# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I feel the bomb's skeleton and nothing more: a display I can't read, a light whose state I can't sense, three wires at fixed positions 1, 2, 3. Everything printed or lit is invisible to me — every bracket in my view is a permanent blank unless someone tells me otherwise.

Tracing the channels before I send anything: I never receive gestures, and Mute cannot speak — so neither Deaf nor Mute can reach me directly with what they see or read. The only voice I can hear is Deaf's, and Deaf hasn't read the manual. So the chain must be: Mute gestures the manual to Deaf, Deaf adds what the bomb looks like, and Deaf *speaks* it to me. My own speech reaches only Mute; my gestures reach both of them.

So this turn: tell Mute exactly what my hands found, what I can do (only cuts, positions 1–3), and how the relay has to work. Meanwhile, gesture to Deaf — Deaf sees gestures — pointing out that I need the visible readouts spoken aloud: the thing on top (display), the thing in the middle (light), the things to the sides (wires), positions one, two, three. Mute will see the same gestures and can back it up with the manual. No cutting until a rule and some actual values arrive.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands found: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I can only cut wires, by position. Colours and printing never reach me, and I never receive gestures, so right now I know nothing beyond that layout. Check the manual for how display, light and wire colours decide the cut. Remember: you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so the only path to me is Deaf's voice. Gesture the rules to Deaf; Deaf can speak and I can hear. I am gesturing to Deaf now to ask for the readouts aloud: display, light, then wire colours in order 1, 2, 3.")
gesture(symbols=["🫵", "🤙", "👆", "👇", "👈", "👉", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report, for both of you: the display reads 0. The light is orange. There are three wires. Left to right: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. There are no other markings or readings on it. Mute, look up what the manual says for this and sign me the instruction. Blind, you have the full picture now from hearing this; the instruction will come from my mouth once Mute signs it to me.

What just landed: Deaf's voice. I now hold the full visible bomb — display 0, orange light, wires red/yellow/blue at positions 1/2/3 — and nothing else. But here's the critical gap I spotted: Deaf spoke that report, and speech only reaches those who can *hear*. Mute can hear, but only Deaf and I were addressed... no wait, Deaf cannot hear, so Deaf's speech reached Mute and me? No — I must re-check: I heard it, so Mute likely heard it too. Either way, the manual side is still dark: Mute has rules but needs to push them through gesture to Deaf, and Deaf alone can speak the verdict to me. I never receive gestures, so "cut N", spoken by Deaf, is the only instruction format I can trust. My job this turn: make sure Mute has the complete bomb state and knows to reduce the rule to a single position number, and give Deaf a tiny gesture code so numbers and yes/no can flow without ambiguity. No cutting until a rule arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. I heard Deaf's report and I pass it to you in full, since you need the bomb state to pick the right manual rule. Display shows the digit 0. Light is orange. Wires, left to right: one red, two yellow, three blue. Nothing else is printed anywhere. My only possible action is cutting one wire at position 1, 2 or 3. Channel map: you hear me and Deaf, but you can only answer by gesture. Deaf hears nobody, so Deaf lives on gestures from you and me, and Deaf can speak to both of us. So the plan: find the rule covering display 0, orange light, red/yellow/blue wires, and boil it down to a single wire position. Keep whatever you sign to Deaf simple: numbers and yes/no checks, so Deaf can verify against the visible bomb and speak me one number. I have just defined a small code to both of you by gesture: fingers for one, two, three; a pinch for cut; thumbs for yes and no.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤏", "👍", "👎", "🫵", "🤏", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update for both of you: the light has changed from orange to green since my last report. The display still reads 0, and all three wires are untouched — red on the left, yellow in the middle, blue on the right. Mute, I received your signs: wave, wire two, yes. Before anyone acts, I need the verb. New code: the OK sign means cut, the fist means press, and thumb-down alone at the end of a message means it is a question. So: is the instruction to cut wire two? And does the light turning green change the manual's answer — thumb-up if cutting wire two still stands, thumb-down if I should expect new signs. Blind, Mute's message concerns wire two, which is the MIDDLE wire of the three you can feel — you cannot see that it is yellow, but it is the one in the middle of your hand. Do not cut or press anything yet. Confirm by feel instead: sign the three-finger sign if you clearly feel a middle wire, and sign anything else you can about what your hands find — I have only told you what I see; whatever your fingers discover, only you can report.

Deaf just gave me three things: the light is now **green** (it was orange — it changes on its own, nobody touched it), the display holds at 0, and Mute's fragmentary sign said something about wire two. Deaf explicitly told me the instruction concerns the MIDDLE wire — position two under my fingers — and asked me to confirm by feel.

My hands confirm it: three wires, the middle one exactly where Deaf says, nothing cut, and — critically — **nothing else I can feel**. Not the display, not the light. I never felt the light change at all. That means Deaf's eyes are the only sensor in this room for both of those, and since the light changes autonomously, Deaf has to watch it continuously and report every change. It also means the rule Mute finds must be a table keyed on light colour, because the state I cut under may differ from the state Deaf observed one round earlier — my cut always lags Deaf's report by a round, so we also need to know how often the light flips.

I will not touch anything: the verb is still unconfirmed and the rule hasn't been re-checked against green. This turn: confirm the middle wire to Deaf in gesture (the three-finger sign Deaf asked for, plus position and an inventory of what my fingers find — all three wires, nothing else), and give Mute the full protocol: answer Deaf with the verb code, build a colour-by-colour decision table, and have Deaf time the light's changes.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Confirmed by feel: I clearly feel three wires, positions one two three, and the middle one — position two — is exactly where Deaf says it is. Nothing else exists for my fingers: I cannot feel the display or the light at all, not even the change Deaf reported. So Deaf's eyes are the only sensor for both, and the light has already flipped orange to green with nobody touching anything, so it will likely flip again. Three things I need from you. First, answer Deaf's question using Deaf's code: OK sign plus two if cutting wire two still stands under a green light, or new signs if the manual says otherwise. Second, build the rule as a table by light colour — for every colour the light can show, which wire I cut, or whether I wait — because my cut lags Deaf's report by one round and the light may change in between. Third, ask Deaf to time the changes: if the light holds steady for long stretches the table is safe; if it flips every few seconds we must catch the pattern first. I have signed Deaf the confirmation: middle wire felt, all three wires intact, nothing else under my fingers. I cut nothing until Deaf speaks the verdict.")
gesture(symbols=["🤟", "✌", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update for both: the light is now RED — it went orange, then green, now red, with nobody touching anything. Display still 0. All three wires intact: red left, yellow middle, blue right.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I read your signs as you counting three distinct wires by touch — that matches my sight exactly: three wires, positions one, two, three. The target so far is the wire in the MIDDLE of the three, position two under your fingers. Do not cut, press, pull or touch anything yet. Answer two yes/no questions by gesture, in this order: first, if you rest your flat hand on the bomb's body, is there a button or plate that gives way — thumb-up — or nothing moves — thumb-down? Second, do the three wires feel different in thickness or texture — thumb-up — or identical — thumb-down? When the action is fully confirmed I will speak it as a complete sentence ending in the word now. Act only when you hear that word.

Two answers to give, and a parsing trap to dodge. My hands say: no button anywhere — resting my palm on the body, the display is just a hard panel, the light just a lens, nothing gives way; and the three wires feel identical except for where they sit — no thickness or texture difference reaches me. Both answers are thumbs-down. But Deaf declared that a thumb-down *alone at the end* of a message means "this is a question" — so if I just send 👎👎, the trailing thumb could be misread as me asking something. I'll append a wave as an end-marker, a symbol Deaf has already parsed correctly once.

The bigger news is the light: orange → green → red, one colour per round, on its own. If the manual rule keys on the light colour at the moment of cutting, then any verdict Deaf speaks to me is already one round stale by the time my pliers close — Mute has to tell me whether the rule cares about the colour at cut-time, the colour sequence, or neither. That determines whether we cut fast or need to sync first. I'm not touching anything until I hear the word "now."

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Urgent: the light is cycling by itself. Deaf reports orange, then green, now red — one colour change per round, nobody touching anything. Display still reads 0. So whatever rule you found must account for timing: does the manual care which colour is showing at the instant of the cut, or the order the colours appear in, or neither? If it cares about the colour at cut time, tell Deaf, because Deaf must speak the verdict AND the light colour together, and I need to know if a change between hearing and cutting voids it. Status of my checks, which I have also signed to Deaf: no button or plate gives way anywhere on the body, and the three wires feel identical by touch — no thickness or texture difference, only position. So position is the only handle I have: one, two, three. Please boil the manual down to one of three numbers, or the word wait, and route it through Deaf to speak as a full sentence ending in the word now. If the answer depends on colour, also give Deaf the mapping so Deaf can adjust the call when the light flips.")
gesture(symbols=["👎", "👎", "👋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for both: the light keeps changing on its own — red has gone back to orange. It seems to cycle: orange, green, red, repeat. Display still 0. Nothing has been touched. Current best understanding: the instruction is to CUT the middle wire, wire two, yellow. Mute's last long message may mean a second step follows — cutting wire three, the right-hand blue wire — but that depends on an undefined sign, so it is unconfirmed. Nobody acts until I say the word now.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I received your answers: nothing on the body gives way when pressed, and all three wires feel identical to the touch. Understood — you will target by position only: the middle wire of the three. The instruction taking shape is to CUT that middle wire, but it is not yet confirmed and you must not cut. Two things now. First, confirm you have a tool that can cut a wire cleanly: thumb-up for yes, thumb-down for no. Second, if yes, position your cutter on the MIDDLE wire of the three and hold it there without closing it. The final go will be a spoken sentence from me ending in the word now. Nothing happens before that word.

Tool check: yes — cutting is the one thing my hands are built for, a clean cut at any position I choose. Deaf also asked me to pre-position on the middle wire and hold without closing. My grip is set on position two right now; the cut itself is a single motion, so "ready" is my permanent state — the instant the word "now" arrives, the cut lands that same round.

But working through the timing exposed a trap: the speaking order is Mute, then me, then Deaf. Deaf speaks **last** in a round, and Deaf's words only reach me at the **start of the next** — by which point the light has advanced one full step in its cycle. So if Deaf ever says "the light is red, cut now," the light I cut under will already be orange. If the manual keys on the colour at cut time, Deaf's go sentence must contain the *predicted* colour for my cutting round, not the colour Deaf sees while speaking. The cycle looks round-locked — exactly one colour change between every pair of Deaf's reports — so prediction is feasible, but Mute must confirm the rule actually cares before we build the protocol around it. Also unresolved: the hinted second cut of wire three, and whether a first cut changes anything visible that Deaf must re-read before step two.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Answered Deaf by sign: tool works, grip resting on the middle wire, position two. The cut is one instant motion, so I fire the same round I hear the word now. Critical timing fact you and Deaf must plan around: Deaf speaks last in a round and I only receive it at the start of the next, and the light advances exactly one colour per round. So the colour I cut under is always ONE STEP PAST whatever Deaf saw while speaking. If the manual cares about the light colour at the instant of cutting, Deaf's go sentence must name the NEXT colour in the cycle, not the current one. Based on the cycle orange green red repeat, Deaf should say something like: the light will be X when you cut, cut two, now. Now four questions, the whole verdict hangs on them. One: is the instruction cut two only, or cut two and then cut three? Two: does any part of the rule depend on light colour at cut time, and if so which colours demand which action or which waiting? Three: does the rule care about the display reading 0 at all? Four: after the first cut, does the manual predict any visible change, so Deaf knows what to re-read before any second step? Please get Deaf the complete final script, every word of it, before the word now is ever spoken. I cut nothing until then.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "✌", "👋"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Decode confirmed for both of you. The complete instruction: cut the middle wire, wire two — and nothing else. No second step; the folded-prayer sign meant nothing; that worry is withdrawn. But the cut must happen while the light is ORANGE. The light has cycled orange, green, red, orange, and is green as I speak — period three, one colour per round. The plan: if the cycle holds, my next report reads red, and the round after that is orange. So in my next message, if and only if the light reads red, I give the go in the same breath. Blind, you cannot see the light — the timing is my responsibility and I have done the arithmetic: the go will reach you at the start of the orange round, and you cut the instant you hear it. Nobody cuts before the word now.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I read your signs: cutting tool yes, positioned on the middle wire, standing by — acknowledged. Hold that exact position, do not close the cutter. The only authorization is a spoken sentence from me ending in the word now — expect it in my very next message. When you hear it, make one clean, immediate, complete cut through the middle wire. If instead my next message says we are holding, keep perfectly still and wait.

The arithmetic checks out, and I traced it end to end before committing my hand to it. Deaf's reports have shown exactly one colour change per round for five straight rounds: round 2 orange, 3 green, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green — a clean period-three cycle. So round 7 is red, round 8 is orange. Deaf speaks the go at the end of round 7, it reaches me at the start of round 8, and I fire in round 8 — while the light is orange. Deaf's plan and my cut land in the same round. My grip is already resting open on wire two; the cut is one motion, so "ready" costs me nothing.

The one residual risk I can't eliminate from the dark: I only know the colour per round, not the flip's exact instant inside a round. But I did find a genuine safety valve in the turn order — Mute speaks **first**, before me, in round 8, the same round I receive the go. So Mute gets one final word that reaches me *before* my hand moves. I'll arm that valve explicitly: silence or "go" means I cut, "hold" means I freeze. Everything else is locked: one cut, wire two, no second step, done. I'm signing Deaf the acknowledgement in Deaf's own code — understood, cut, two, end.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf's go arrives with the next report and my cut fires instantly, in the round after this one, which the cycle says will be orange: the observed sequence orange green red orange green pins this round as red and my cutting round as orange. Two last things before I commit. First, if the manual gives any hint that the cycle can stutter, or that a cut made slightly off-phase is survivable, say it now. Second, a safety valve built into the turn order: in the round I receive the go, your voice reaches me BEFORE my hand moves, because you speak first. So in that round: if you are fully confident in the instruction, say nothing or say the word go, and I cut wire two on Deaf's now. If anything at all is wrong, say the word hold and I will not cut. After the cut I will report what my fingers find, wire two severed, and Deaf can confirm visually. This is the final round of questions. If the instruction is exactly one cut, the middle wire, while the light is orange, no second step, then we are done talking and I am ready.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👌", "✌", "👋"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Go. All confirmations are in. Mute's final answer was thumb-up: the cut must happen while the light is orange. And the light reads red right now, exactly as the cycle predicted — orange, green, red has now repeated in full, so the next round is orange, and these words reach you at the start of it. Blind, this is the authorization, complete: make one clean, immediate, complete cut through the MIDDLE wire of the three — wire two, the yellow one, the middle one under your fingers — while the light is orange, and after the cut take your hands off the bomb entirely. Cut it now.

The word has arrived, and every gate on my side is green. Gate one — authorization: Deaf's complete sentence, ending in "now." Gate two — the phase: Deaf verified the full cycle has repeated exactly, orange-green-red twice through, this round reads red at speaking time, so the round these words land in is orange — and my cut fires this round, under orange, exactly what Mute's thumb-up demanded. Gate three — the safety valve: Mute speaks before me every round, and if Mute had wanted a hold, that word would have reached me in this same batch. Nothing came. Per the armed agreement, silence means go.

My grip is already resting open on the middle wire of three. I close the cutter — one clean, immediate, complete cut through wire two — and then my hands leave the bomb entirely, as instructed. I report the action to both: spoken to Mute, signed to Deaf in our code (cut, two, done), asking Deaf to visually confirm the wire is severed and to keep watching the light and display for any change. No second step exists; the instruction was one cut, and it is done.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. The go arrived, no hold came from you, so per our valve agreement I made one clean cut through wire two, the middle wire, this round — the round Deaf's arithmetic and the twice-repeated cycle both pin as orange. My hands are now off the bomb entirely. Please check the manual one last time: after a correct single cut of the middle wire under an orange light, is there anything left to do, any expected change, or is the bomb defused? Tell Deaf what to look for and speak the outcome to me. Standing by, touching nothing.")
gesture(symbols=["👌", "✌", "👋"])
```
